claims.statement: Mike McCoole was matched to fight Tom Allen for $1,000 on March 17 within 60 miles of St. Louis; articles were signed and a $150 forfeit put up.
claims.excerpt:
Mike McCoole, “Champion of
America,” was matched to tight Tom Allen, of Eng-
land, for one thousand dollars, on the 17th ‘arch.

claims.statement: Tom Allen sparred Mike McCoole earnestly in the windup of the Saturday night exhibition, and McCoole bled from a reopened cut on his forehead.
claims.excerpt:
In the wind-up, the set-to between McCoole and Allen was char-
acterized by a determination and earnestness seldom
witnessed in a friendly contest.

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Bill Ryall had been in St. Louis only a few weeks when this was printed.
claims.excerpt:
They
have been in the city but a few weeks

claims.statement: Mike McCoole, after withdrawing from the Allen match, offered to fight Allen for $2,500 ninety days after his fight with Joe Coburn.
claims.excerpt:
He is willing to fight Allen for $2,500
ninety days after his it with Coburn

fights.excerpt:
Mike McCoole, “Champion of
America,” was matched to tight Tom Allen, of Eng-
land, for one thousand dollars, on the 17th ‘arch.
fights.notes: Planned bout, never fought. Articles signed 1868-03-07 with a $150 forfeit; McCoole withdrew 1868-03-08 at his friends' urging. The text does not say who lost the $150, so 'forfeit' is inferred from the withdrawal.

notes: The McCoole exhibition and the match were both on Saturday 1868-03-07. The OCR is heavily damaged in places.
